```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = if (dir.exists("data")) "." else "..")
library(pliman)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
#| label: images
#| include: false
soy     <- image_pliman("soy_green.jpg", plot = FALSE)
touch   <- image_pliman("soybean_touch.jpg", plot = FALSE)
objects <- image_pliman("objects_300dpi.jpg", plot = FALSE)
leaves  <- image_pliman("la_leaves.jpg", plot = FALSE)
flax    <- image_pliman("flax_grains.jpg", plot = FALSE)
fleaves <- image_pliman("flax_leaves.jpg", plot = FALSE)
shadow  <- image_pliman("shadow.jpg", plot = FALSE)
```

## Plan for the afternoon

| Block | Topic |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| 1 | From a photograph to a number |
| 2 | Taking images that can be analysed |
| 3 | Counting, measuring and scale with `pliman` |
| 4 | Colour, leaves and disease severity |
| 5 | Many images at once, and is the trait good enough? |
| 6 | Near infrared and drones (briefly), exercise and discussion |

::: keybox
**Goal:** leave able to turn a photograph taken with a phone into trait values for a trial, and to check that those values can be trusted.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Block 1 {.divider}

From a photograph to a number

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## An image is a table of numbers

1. **Capture** under controlled conditions
2. **Segment**: separate seeds, leaves or lesions from the background
3. **Measure**: count, size, shape, colour
4. **Tabulate**: one row per plot, with the plot identifier
5. **Analyse**: the table enters the same workflow as any other trait (Days 3 and 4)

::: keybox
High-throughput phenotyping does not need expensive equipment: a phone, a tray and R are enough to start.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Low-cost platforms

| Platform | Typical use |
|:--------------|:-----------------------------------------------|
| Smartphone, stand and plain tray | Seed number, size and colour; leaf area; disease on detached leaves |
| Flatbed scanner | Seeds, grains, leaves, roots; known resolution (dpi) |
| Fixed RGB camera on a frame | Canopy cover and greenness of a plot, over time |
| Camera modified for near infrared | Indices that need NIR (NDVI) |
| Drone with RGB or multispectral camera | Plant height, canopy cover and vigour of the whole trial |

[From the cheapest to the most expensive. Drones: only briefly, at the end.]{.small-note}

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Block 2 {.divider}

Taking images that can be analysed

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Most of the work is before the photograph

| Decision | What to do |
|:-----------|:------------------------------------------------------|
| Background | One plain colour that the objects do not have |
| Light | Even and diffuse, the same for all images; no direct sun |
| Scale | A reference object of known size in every image, or a known dpi |
| Objects | Separated, flat, not overlapping |
| File name | The plot identifier: `plot_101.jpg` |
| Camera | Same camera and settings; keep the original files |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What uneven light does

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.6
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(shadow)
invisible(analyze_objects(shadow, plot = TRUE, show_original = FALSE, verbose = FALSE))
```

- Left: a leaf with a shadow on the background. Right: the default mask
- The shadow is read as part of the object and half of the leaf is lost
- No setting repairs this reliably: **fix it at capture**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Block 3 {.divider}

Counting, measuring and scale with `pliman`

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Setting up

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("pliman")        # in the course installation
BiocManager::install("EBImage")   # also required: from Bioconductor
library(pliman)
```

::: keybox
If `library(pliman)` prints "Package EBImage is required", the Bioconductor step is missing.
:::

- All images today are the **sample images** installed with `pliman` (Olivoto 2022)
- `image_pliman("name.jpg")` reads them: the examples run on any computer

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## An image and an index

```{r}
dim(soy)      # height, width, and three colour channels
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 2.7
image_index(soy, index = c("R", "GLI", "NGRDI"), ncol = 3, nrow = 1)
```

- A **vegetation index** combines the channels in one number that highlights something
- GLI is high for green tissue; NGRDI separates green from yellow and red
- We choose the index that separates what we want, and check it on a few images

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Counting seeds

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.6
seeds <- analyze_objects(touch, marker = "id", verbose = FALSE)
```

```{r}
seeds$statistics[1:3, ]
```

::: keybox
**30 seeds**, touching seeds separated. We counted the labels one by one: correct. Every automatic count needs this check.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What is measured

```{r}
seeds$results |>
  select(id, area, perimeter, length, width, circularity) |>
  head(5)
```

- More than thirty measurements per object: area, perimeter, length, width, shape descriptors
- All in **pixels**. To compare images we need a **scale**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Scale 1: a known resolution (dpi)

```{r}
obj <- analyze_objects(objects, verbose = FALSE)
cm  <- as.data.frame(unclass(get_measures(obj, dpi = 300)))
cm |> select(id, area, width, length)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
sq <- cm[1, ]
```

::: keybox
`objects_300dpi.jpg` contains a square of 10 x 10 cm. The software finds `r round(sq$width, 2)` x `r round(sq$length, 2)` cm, `r round(sq$area, 1)` cm²: an error of about 0.3%. **Validate with something of known size.**
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Scale 2: a reference object

```{r}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5
la <- analyze_objects(leaves, marker = "id", reference = TRUE,
                      reference_area = 4, reference_smaller = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
```

```{r}
la$results |> select(id, area, length, width)
```

- A square of 2 x 2 cm (4 cm²) travels with the sample: areas in cm² at any distance or camera

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Many small seeds

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.8
fx <- analyze_objects(flax, index = "GRAY", reference = TRUE, reference_area = 6,
                      reference_larger = TRUE, show_contour = FALSE, marker = "point",
                      verbose = FALSE)
fx_noise <- analyze_objects(flax, index = "GRAY", reference = TRUE, reference_area = 6,
                            reference_larger = TRUE, lower_noise = 0.3, plot = FALSE,
                            verbose = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
analyze_objects(flax, index = "GRAY", reference = TRUE, reference_area = 6,
                reference_larger = TRUE)
```

::: keybox
`r nrow(fx$results)` seeds. With `lower_noise = 0.3` the same image gives `r nrow(fx_noise$results)`: **a parameter can change the count.** Look at the labelled image of a few samples before running a batch.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Block 4 {.divider}

Colour, leaves and disease severity

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Colour as a trait

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 3.2
colour <- analyze_objects(soy, marker = "id", object_index = c("NGRDI", "GLI"),
                          verbose = FALSE)
```

```{r}
colour$object_index |> mutate(across(-id, \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

- Seeds 5 and 9 are greener: higher GLI, NGRDI close to zero

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Classifying by a threshold

```{r}
colour$object_index |>
  mutate(class = if_else(NGRDI > -0.05, "green", "yellow")) |>
  count(class)
```

::: keybox
The threshold must come from **data**: fix it on seeds classified by an expert, check it on another set. If colour is a **proxy** (yellow intensity for carotenoids), calibrate against laboratory values and test on new samples. That is a prediction problem: tomorrow's machine learning session.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Elongated objects: the flax leaves

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
split_default <- analyze_objects(fleaves, marker = "id", verbose = FALSE)
whole <- analyze_objects(fleaves, marker = "id", watershed = FALSE,
                         object_index = c("NGRDI", "GLI"), verbose = FALSE)
```

- **Left:** default settings, `r nrow(split_default$results)` objects: the *watershed* cuts long leaves in pieces
- **Right:** `watershed = FALSE`, `r nrow(whole$results)` objects: one per leaf
- Now we can measure and classify

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## A senescence score

```{r}
whole$results |>
  select(id, area, length, width) |>
  left_join(whole$object_index, by = "id") |>
  mutate(yellow = NGRDI < 0) |>
  filter(yellow)
```

::: keybox
Two of the 15 leaves have NGRDI below zero: the two yellow ones. The same logic gives a **stay-green** or **senescence** score without a colour chart.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Disease severity

```{r}
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 3.6
set.seed(10)
leaf    <- image_pliman("sev_leaf_nb.jpg", plot = FALSE)
healthy <- image_pliman("sev_healthy.jpg", plot = FALSE)
lesions <- image_pliman("sev_sympt.jpg", plot = FALSE)
sev <- measure_disease(img = leaf, img_healthy = healthy, img_symptoms = lesions,
                       lesion_size = "large", plot = TRUE)
```

```{r}
sev$severity
```

- Three palettes define "healthy" and "symptom": use the **same palettes** for the whole study
- Useful to screen large M2 populations without rating each leaf by eye

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Block 5 {.divider}

Many images at once, and is the trait good enough?

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## A folder of images

```{r}
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "plots")
dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
src <- system.file("tmp_images", package = "pliman")
invisible(file.copy(file.path(src, c("soybean_touch.jpg", "soy_green.jpg", "flax_grains.jpg")),
                    file.path(dir, c("plot_101.jpg", "plot_102.jpg", "plot_103.jpg"))))

batch <- analyze_objects(pattern = "plot_", dir_original = dir, plot = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
batch$statistics
```

[The three images only show the structure: they are not three plots of a trial.]{.small-note}

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Join with the trial

```{r}
#| eval: false
# 'trial' is the field book: one row per plot, with the column "plot"
image_traits <- batch$statistics |>
  mutate(plot = as.integer(sub("plot_", "", img))) |>
  select(plot, seed_number = n, seed_area = area_mean)

trial <- trial |> left_join(image_traits, by = "plot")
```

::: keybox
From here the image traits are **traits like any other**: they go to the single-trial analysis of this morning (mixed model, spatial correction if justified), and their heritability tells us if they are precise enough to select on.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Is the image trait good enough?

- **Valid:** it agrees with the manual or laboratory measurement on a subset of plots (20 to 50 is a start)
- **Precise:** its heritability in the trial is high enough to select on
- **Reproducible:** two photographs of the same sample give the same value

```{r}
#| eval: false
cor(check$seed_number_image, check$seed_number_manual)
plot(check$seed_number_manual, check$seed_number_image); abline(0, 1)
```

::: keybox
Distance from the line `abline(0, 1)` that is the same for all samples is a **bias** that can be corrected. Scatter around it is **error** that cannot.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Near infrared and drones, briefly

**Near infrared.** Healthy leaves reflect much more NIR than visible red. A camera with the infrared filter removed, or a multispectral camera, records it. NDVI measures vigour and stress better than RGB indices.

**Drones.** Images are joined in an orthomosaic, the field is divided in plots with a shapefile, and indices are extracted per plot: again one row per plot. `pliman` has `mosaic_*` functions for this.

::: keybox
For a programme that is starting: learn the steps of this session with photographs on a tray first. Segmentation, scale, validation and the join with the trial are the same.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Pitfalls

| Pitfall | What to do |
|:--------------------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| Uneven light or shadows | Diffuse light, same set-up in all images |
| One set of parameters for all images | Test on 5 to 10 images, then keep them |
| No scale | Reference object or known dpi |
| Not looking at the labelled image | Inspect the labelled image of a sample |
| Colour threshold from 9 seeds | Fix on a training set, check on another |
| Image trait without validation | Compare with manual measurements |
| Different cameras between trials | Same camera and settings; keep the originals |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Exercise

With the image `flax_leaves.jpg`:

1. Count the leaves with the default settings and with `watershed = FALSE`. Which one is correct?
2. Get the length and the width of each leaf, in pixels
3. Which leaves have the lowest NGRDI? How many, and in which row of the picture?
4. With `flax_grains.jpg`: total seed area in cm². Why does it change with `lower_noise = 0.3`?

::: keybox
Hint: `whole$results`, `whole$object_index` and `fx$results` have what you need.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Questions for discussion

- Which trait of your programme is measured by eye today and could be measured from a photograph?
- What would you put in the photograph as reference object, and on which background?
- How would you validate the image trait before using it for selection?
- Where would an image trait help in the M2 and M3 generations, when populations are large?

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Key takeaways

- An image is a table of numbers: segment, measure, tabulate, analyse
- A good photograph (plain background, even light, reference object, plot as file name) is worth more than any option in the software
- `pliman` counts, measures size and shape, describes colour and severity, for one image or a folder
- **Validate** with something of known size; **look** at the labelled image before trusting a batch
- A colour proxy needs a laboratory calibration; an image trait must be valid and heritable
- Start with a phone and a tray
